The tail is a path hanging off one node of the clique." width="100%"} Creates a complete graph ("candy") of `m` nodes with a path ("stick") of `n` more nodes hanging off one of them. The graph has `m + n` nodes and `m(m - 1)/2 + n` edges. With `n=0` it is just the complete graph. The clique is created first and the stick follows, attached to the clique's last node, so the far end of the stick is the last node created. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one, so the stick points away from the clique. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Lollipop graphs are classic extreme cases: - random walks: with `m` about `2(m + n)/3`, a walk started in the clique takes the longest possible expected time (of order `(m + n)^3`) to reach the end of the stick - mixing a dense core and a long periphery in one test graph, e.g. for centrality, k-core, or eccentricity measures - checking that path-based measures handle a long tail correctly ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [m]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the clique. Must be at least `2`. [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes on the stick. Must be non-negative. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `m=` is less than `2` or `n=` is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A four-node clique with a three-node stick has `7` nodes and `6 + 3 = 9` edges: ::: {#aab2abb4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_lollipop_graph(m=4, n=3) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (7, 9) ``` ::: ::: The stick hangs from node `"4"`, the clique's last node, so the longest shortest path runs from the clique to the tip `"7"`: ::: {#e9e7f609 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.diameter(), graph.get_degree("4"), graph.get_degree("7") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (4, 4, 1) ``` ::: :::
